newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares fall 2.0 pct on mutual fund sales.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares fall 2.0 pct on mutual fund sales.

text.p: Israeli shares closed sharply lower on Thursday in thin trading amid sales by mutual funds, traders said.
"Activity is low and the mood in the market is negative. In the near future the market will continue to decline because investors are moving to more attractive investments," a trader said.
"Everything depends now on progress made in the Middle East peace process. If there's no breakthrough in the talks the market has no future," he said.
Israeli-Palestinian talks were renewed this week following recent clashes that killed 74 people.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 2.03 percent, or 3.76 points, to 181.68 on low turnover of 54 million shekels against 40 million on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 2.12 percent to 191.05.

"Activity rose slightly today but the fact that the market is falling on higher volume is a bad sign. The main sellers were the big mutual funds and this had a very negative impact on trading," said Ari Eidelhet at Central Securities Corp.
"With such a low turnover every big seller affects the market immediately," Eidelhet said.
Blue Square Chain closed unchanged at 2,411. UBS rated the company a "buy", noting they are trading at a large discount to its parent, traded on the New York Stock Exchange.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 1.75 percent to 138,868 on volume of 4.7 million shekels; Koor Industries, which lost 2.0 percent to 27,008 on volume of 3.5 million shekels; and Bank Hapoalim, which fell 1.0 percent to 434 on turnover of 2.8 million shekels.
